version.changelog:
openmaic v0.3.13

- Updated the provider keys reference (references/provider-keys.md) with new or revised guidance.
- Removed the skill card documentation (skill-card.md) from the skill.

llm.summary: The skill is a disclosed OpenMAIC setup and generation guide; it uses network calls, local config, and uploads in ways that match that purpose.

dimensions.detail: The skill may send requirements, uploaded materials, and an access code to OpenMAIC endpoints, or to a user-selected local URL. This is proportionate for classroom generation, but users should treat uploaded files as shared with the configured service.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill package itself is Markdown-only. It may guide users to clone OpenMAIC, run pnpm/npm installs, Docker Compose, or builds, with confirmation requirements.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions require confirmation before state-changing actions and before reading local files for upload. Stored Live Demo access codes are used directly from skill config, but the host and purpose are disclosed.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No cron jobs, startup hooks, tool hijacking, hidden persistence, or backdoor behavior were found. Persistence is limited to user-managed config, cookie jars, local databases/containers, and server-side generation state described in the docs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill helps users run or use OpenMAIC, configure provider keys, generate classrooms, and extend the SDK/product. Network API calls, file uploads, package installs, and local service startup are coherent with that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with OpenMAIC receiving the classroom requirement, any uploaded materials, and the Live Demo access code when using open.maic.chat. Keep API keys in local config or the web app as directed, review commands before approving installs or Docker startup, and avoid uploading sensitive documents unless the configured OpenMAIC service is appropriate for them.
llm.findings:
[TM1] expected: The cited git clean text is a warning about what happens if a user has already cleaned the repo; it is not an instruction to run the destructive command.
[PE3] expected: .env.local is used for the user's own OpenMAIC provider keys. The skill explicitly tells the user to edit key files themselves and not paste keys into chat.
[RA2] unexpected: The cited text does not establish unauthorized persistence; it says not to write API keys for the user and avoids duplicate confirmation only after the user has already requested generation.
[E1] expected: External POST/GET examples are the documented OpenMAIC API flow. Local file reads for upload require confirmation, and the destination is the configured OpenMAIC URL or the disclosed Live Demo host.
[SQP-2] expected: Using a stored access code is expected for Live Demo mode and the host is fixed to open.maic.chat. Users should still understand that the token is sent as an Authorization header.
[EA2] expected: The no-second-confirmation instruction is scoped to generation after the user has clearly asked to generate. Other state-changing actions remain covered by confirmation rules.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese terms appear in the secondary-development documentation and product UI references, but the artifact does not require a hidden locale or force unrelated language behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: The remote font note is disclosed for SDK consumers. It can cause outbound font requests when consumers import the renderer font CSS, but this is documented rather than hidden.
